## Purpose and Entrypoint
Fincept Terminal is a native, cross-platform financial intelligence and trading desktop application. Its primary runtime is C++20/Qt6; embedded Python supplies analytics, data connectors, agent implementations, and exchange tooling. Application startup is `fincept-qt/src/app/main.cpp`, which leads into the terminal/window shell in `fincept-qt/src/app/TerminalShell.cpp` and `fincept-qt/src/app/WindowFrame.cpp`.

## Desktop Shell and Workspace Runtime
The Qt desktop shell routes screens, materializes dockable panels, and maintains multi-monitor/window layouts. Core shared services are centralized behind a service locator and event bus, separating UI screens from domain services. User profiles, screen state, layouts, symbol linking, and crash recovery form the local-session boundary.
- `fincept-qt/src/app/DockScreenRouter.cpp`
- `fincept-qt/src/core/services/Services.cpp`
- `fincept-qt/src/core/layout/WorkspaceShell.cpp`

## Local Persistence, Security, and Sync
SQLite-backed repositories persist portfolios, workflows, chat, dashboards, feeds, configurations, and trading state; migrations define the evolving local schema. Secure storage holds sensitive credentials. Cloud synchronization is adapter-based, allowing selected local domains to synchronize through the cloud client while retaining local repositories as the application boundary.
- `fincept-qt/src/storage/sqlite/Database.cpp`
- `fincept-qt/src/storage/sqlite/migrations/MigrationRunner.cpp`
- `fincept-qt/src/services/cloud/CloudSyncEngine.cpp`

## Data Ingestion and Distribution
External financial, economic, government, news, and alternative-data sources are largely invoked through Python scripts. C++ services/screens consume results and publish live or derived data through `DataHub`, whose producer/topic abstractions provide a common in-process streaming boundary. HTTP and WebSocket wrappers support C++-native integrations.
- `fincept-qt/src/datahub/DataHub.cpp`
- `fincept-qt/src/python/PythonRunner.cpp`
- `fincept-qt/scripts/yfinance_data.py`

## Trading and Execution Boundary
Trading screens and services work through broker/exchange abstractions rather than directly binding UI to a venue. Account/session managers, data streams, order validation, paper trading, and smart-order logic coordinate the execution path. Concrete adapters cover named brokers plus Hyperliquid; Python exchange daemons provide another exchange integration path. This is the material boundary for real-money credentials and order submission.
- `fincept-qt/src/trading/UnifiedTrading.cpp`
- `fincept-qt/src/trading/BrokerRegistry.cpp`
- `fincept-qt/src/trading/SmartOrderEngine.cpp`

## Analytics, Backtesting, and Algo Execution
The app exposes analytics, portfolio, derivatives, options, strategy, and AI quant interfaces backed by Python modules and native engines. The C++ algo engine handles candles, indicators, scanning, backtesting, positions, and deployments; Python offers multiple backtesting providers and quantitative-library wrappers. Strategy examples and the internal strategy framework support executable research/deployment flows.
- `fincept-qt/src/algo_engine/AlgoEngine.cpp`
- `fincept-qt/scripts/Analytics/backtesting/base/fincept_strategy_runner.py`
- `fincept-qt/scripts/strategies/fincept_engine/algorithm.py`

## AI, MCP, and Visual Workflows
LLM providers are mediated by a native LLM service, while MCP exposes terminal capabilities as validated tools. Agent configurations and Python runtimes support personas, planning, memory, tools, and paper-trading bridges. The node-editor UI defines workflows that are executed by a registry-driven workflow service with confirmation, risk, audit, and service-bridge stages.
- `fincept-qt/src/services/llm/LlmService.cpp`
- `fincept-qt/src/mcp/McpManager.cpp`
- `fincept-qt/src/services/workflow/WorkflowExecutor.cpp`

## Build, Packaging, and External Dependencies
CMake builds the C++ binary with Qt6; Python 3.11+ is an embedded/managed companion runtime. Docker is intended for Linux/X11 development or CI. Deliverables include Flatpak, Linux AppImage, and installer configurations. External dependencies include broker APIs, market/economic data APIs, LLM providers, MCP servers, cloud endpoints, and optional wallet/Solana RPC connectivity.
- `fincept-qt/CMakeLists.txt`
- `Dockerfile`
- `fincept-qt/packaging/linux/AppImageBuilder.yml`
